ai.description: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* is a small skink reaching 40–50 mm. It is bronze-brown with a distinct pale dorsolateral stripe and lacks functional eyelids. The limbs are reduced with five digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, pale dorsolateral stripes and a lack of dark spotting on the flanks, unlike the similar *A. grayanus*.
ai.habitat: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky slopes in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 4,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–3 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ablepharus tragbulensis* is found in the high-altitude regions of the Western Himalayas, specifically within Jammu and Kashmir, typically occurring above 2,000 meters.
